<thought>By examining the 13C NMR peaks, the signals in the typical aromatic region (≈110–150 ppm) are at 144.78, 132.00, two at 130.07, and two at 127.80 ppm. That gives a total of 6 distinct aromatic carbon signals. The remaining peaks correspond to carbonyl, aliphatic, and methyl carbons. Therefore, the molecule contains 6 aromatic carbon atoms.</thought>
<final_answer>6</final_answer>
